content: Multiple 2026 sources (digitalapplied.com, encore.dev 'you-probably-dont-need-a-vector-database', teachmeidea.com) converge: pgvector in the primary Postgres DB is sufficient for RAG at small-to-medium scale — documents and chunk embeddings live in the same transactional DB as application data, eliminating a sync problem between separate stores. Standard RAG shape: documents table (raw rulebook text/metadata) -> chunks table (chunk_text, embedding vector, document_id FK, chunk_index) with fixed-size or recursive chunking (~500 chars is a commonly cited starting point) -> retrieval is a single SQL query (optionally hybrid FTS+vector) -> top-k chunks injected into LLM prompt. Elixir-side prior art: rag_ex (nshkrdotcom) implements this exact pgvector-backed chunking+retrieval pipeline with pluggable LLM routing including Gemini.
